images.observation: Trigger cap lifted above motor; attachment structure visible, no calibrated scale.
Cap removed; metal motor body and eccentric weight visible, with a coil spring near the shoulder. Photograph does not establish spring rate or a metric hinge frame.
Contact region between trigger and white frame highlighted; image alone does not establish pad thickness or material parameters.

model_requirements: Distinguish exterior cap geometry from full moving assembly. If internal components are aggregated into one link, its mass and inertia must represent that assembly, not a uniform-density visual cap.
Represent or explicitly mark unresolved frame-to-trigger stop contact. Do not silently claim an ideal joint limit reproduces a compliant cushion.
Do not infer gameplay hinge axes from cap-removal directions.
Rumble actuation may remain disabled for passive manipulation; documenting the motor's inertial contribution does not require inventing powered vibration behavior.
validation: Downloaded image hashes recorded and all three images visually inspected. No photogrammetry, dimensional fit, force measurement or dynamic contact validation performed.
future_harness: When geometry and parameters exist: sweep each trigger through its configured range, record stop contact separation/penetration and moving-assembly inertia; compare loading and release curves independently. Not yet implemented or passed.
adoption: Cross-model qualitative structure reference only. No Xbox One S mechanism fact or numerical target parameter is adopted; source screw-size text is excluded from scale calibration. Applicability requires a target teardown or direct mechanism comparison.
reuse: Third-party reference photographs retained on GPU, not redistributed as mesh textures.
